stem: A female transplant recipient asks about intrauterine device (IUD) contraception after transplantation. Which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Counsel about increased infection risk with intrauterine devices
Intrauterine devices have no infection risk in immunosuppressed recipients
Intrauterine devices are the only recommended contraceptive method after transplant
Infection risk counseling applies only to male recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Sexual health teaching includes counseling recipients about increased risk of infection with intrauterine devices along with other contraception and pregnancy planning topics.

rationale_incorrect.B: Increased infection risk with intrauterine devices is specifically cited for counseling.
rationale_incorrect.C: Multiple contraceptive options are discussed rather than intrauterine devices alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Intrauterine device counseling applies to female recipients.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → k. Sexual health → vi.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Counsel recipients about increased risk of infection with intrauterine devices

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → k. Sexual health → vi. (increased infection risk with IUDs); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. IUD infection-risk angle distinct from oral-contraception counseling (cctc-1123) and condom teaching (cctc-1122); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.

stem: When teaching sexual health after transplantation, which counseling point about libido aligns with standard references?

options.text: Sexual dysfunction or changes in libido may be related to medications; encourage open communication with providers
Libido changes never occur after transplantation
Sexual concerns should never be discussed with the transplant team
All libido changes require permanent discontinuation of immunosuppression

explanation.rationale_correct: Sexual health teaching notes that sexual dysfunction or changes in libido may be related to medications and encourages patients to openly communicate concerns to healthcare providers.

rationale_incorrect.B: Medication-related sexual dysfunction and libido changes may occur.
rationale_incorrect.C: Open communication with healthcare providers is encouraged.
rationale_incorrect.D: Concerns are addressed through counseling and medication review rather than automatic cessation of all immunosuppression.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → k. Sexual health → vii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Sexual dysfunction or changes in libido may be related to medications … openly communicate their concerns to healthcare providers

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → k. Sexual health → vii. (libido changes may relate to medications; encourage provider communication); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Libido/sexual-dysfunction teaching angle distinct from appearance changes (cctc-1124) and pregnancy counseling (cctc-1091); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.

stem: After a transplant recipient becomes pregnant or a male recipient fathers a child, which referral aligns with standard references?

options.text: No registry referral is ever recommended for transplant pregnancy outcomes
Referral only to a local blood bank registry
Pregnancy registry referral applies only before transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Pregnant recipients and males who have fathered a child after transplantation should be referred to the National Transplant Pregnancy Registry.

rationale_incorrect.B: Registry referral is recommended for pregnancy and fatherhood after transplant.
rationale_incorrect.C: The National Transplant Pregnancy Registry is the cited referral resource.
rationale_incorrect.D: Referral occurs after pregnancy or fathering a child rather than only pretransplant.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → l. Pregnancy after transplantation → iv.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Refer pregnant recipients and males who have fathered a child to the National Transplant Pregnancy Registry

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → l. Pregnancy after transplantation → iv. (National Transplant Pregnancy Registry referral); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Pregnancy-registry referral angle distinct from pregnancy-timing counseling (cctc-1091) and reproductive-health combo (cctc-1125); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.

stem: A coordinator is updating contraception and sexual-health teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Emergency contraception may be considered in certain circumstances.
Recipients should be counseled about increased infection risk with intrauterine devices.
Sexual dysfunction or libido changes should never be discussed with healthcare providers.
Oral contraception should be discussed with the provider because of thromboembolic risk.

explanation.rationale_correct: Emergency contraception, intrauterine device infection risk, and provider discussion of oral contraception are supported. Statement III is false because open communication about sexual dysfunction and libido is encouraged.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—oral contraception requires provider discussion due to thromboembolic risk.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because provider communication about sexual concerns is encouraged.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → k. Sexual health
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Emergency contraception … increased risk of infection with intrauterine devices … openly communicate … oral contraception … thromboembolic events

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → k. Sexual health → iv.–vii. (emergency contraception, IUD risk, libido communication, oral contraception thromboembolic risk); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Contraception/sexual-health combo distinct from reproductive-health combo (cctc-1125) and condom recall (cctc-1122); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.
